title: MapSpec v1 build-time rules and acceptance test vectors
description: Plain rules data file (NOT a JSON Schema). Non-schema enforcement rules for build-html.mjs, separated from mapspec-v1.schema.json so that schema stays clean for strict validators (ajv strict mode rejects unknown keywords). These are runtime/build-time checks, consumed by build-html.mjs unit tests; not validated by ajv.

pathValidation.description: evidence.path must be relative to the user-confirmed evidence root (--repo-root): the repository root for code maps, or the documents directory for non-code business-process maps. Regex in schema rejects empty/absolute/drive/UNC; segment-level rules below are enforced in build-html.mjs since regex cannot express them.
rules: Reject if path contains backslash '\'
After splitting on '/', reject if any segment is '..' or '.'
Reject if path resolves outside the user-confirmed evidence root

evidenceRangeValidation.description: When both lineStart and lineEnd are present, build-html.mjs must enforce lineEnd >= lineStart. Schema's if/then already requires verified evidence to carry both line numbers.
rules: If lineStart and lineEnd present, lineEnd must be >= lineStart
verified evidence requires non-empty relative path + lineStart + lineEnd (enforced by schema if/then)

displayPathPrivacy.description: All displayable MapSpec strings (meta, titles, labels, notes and detail cells) must not contain a user-local absolute filesystem path. evidence.path is governed by the stricter relative-path contract above. The runtime check recognizes Unix user/system roots, Windows drive paths and UNC paths; URL syntax is allowed.
rules: Reject /Users/<name>, /home/<name>, /root, /private, /Volumes, /var, /etc, /tmp, /opt, /Library, /usr, /bin, /sbin, /dev, /proc, /sys, /run, /boot, /mnt, /media, /srv, /System, /Applications or /Network path forms in displayable strings
Reject Windows drive paths and UNC paths in displayable strings
Do not treat a normal HTTP(S) URL as a filesystem path

codeExcerptLimits.description: A code segment is bounded to keep the generated standalone HTML reviewable and to prevent unbounded excerpt embedding.
rules: Apply these limits only when detail.segments[].kind is code
Schema enforces maxRows and maxCellChars; the runtime validator enforces all three limits including maxSegmentChars

mermaidDslInjectionValidation.description: All text entering the Mermaid DSL — node titles, edge labels, subgraph titles (nodes[].subgraph) — is untrusted. build-html.mjs must encode them to literal text and use internally-generated safe IDs for subgraphs. These vectors verify the encoder. Asserting only 'mustNotChangeDsl' is insufficient — trivially dropping the malicious title could pass; each vector asserts structure-preserved + literal-visible + safe-id.
rules: subgraph uses internally-generated safe ID (e.g. sg1, sg2), user text only as display label
Encode characters that alter DSL structure: 'end', newline, quotes, %%{...}, -->/---
Structure preserved: number of nodes/edges/subgraphs in rendered output matches input MapSpec
Literal visible: the input text (after encoding) still appears as literal display text, not dropped
Safe id: subgraph statement uses internal id, not the user text

sensitiveDataRejection.description: P1-4 (v3.2.12): security contract forbids .env/keys/credentials in HTML, but rules previously did not reject them. validate.mjs and build-html.mjs MUST reject sensitive paths and sensitive content. Patterns are a heuristic early-warning (v3.2.14): not an absolute guarantee of no leakage; the final HTML post-scan MUST reuse the SAME rule set exported by skill/renderer/validate-map-spec.mjs. Vectors in tests/mapspec/fixtures/invalid/.
sensitiveDataRejection.htmlPostScan: build-html.mjs MUST re-scan the final HTML with the SAME rule set exported by validate-map-spec.mjs (import isSensitivePath/isSensitiveContent/containsAbsoluteFilesystemPath); reject on match.

verifiedEvidenceFileValidation.description: P0 (v3.2.14): state=verified evidence must trace back to code or documents that were actually inspected. When --repo-root is provided, build-html.mjs MUST enforce: repo root exists and is a directory; each verified evidence.path resolves (realpath) to a real regular file inside the root; lineStart/lineEnd are within the file's actual line count (counted by '\n', CRLF-safe). Missing files, directories, out-of-range lines, symlink escapes and root-is-a-file are rejected. inferred/unconfirmed evidence does NOT require the file to exist (they are not 'verified'), but still must pass relative-path and sensitive rules.
rules: repo root must exist and be a directory
verified evidence.path must realpath to a real regular file inside the root (symlink escape rejected)
verified evidence lineEnd must be <= actual file line count (\n count, CRLF-safe)
inferred/unconfirmed evidence: file existence not required
acceptanceTestVectors: path pointing to a directory -> reject
lineEnd beyond file line count -> reject
CRLF file line count correct -> pass within range, reject beyond
repo root is a regular file -> reject
inferred evidence with nonexistent path -> pass
NUL byte in evidence path -> reject (no exception)

newline-only file line count: '
' counts 1 line, '

' counts 2 lines (trailing empty segment removed) -> pass within range, reject beyond

sequenceDiagramContract.description: Rules for meta.diagramKind=sequence that JSON Schema cannot express (code-point counting, cross-message pairing, DSL-context text contracts). Enforced by skill/renderer/validate-map-spec.mjs and the sequence DSL generator. Locked contracts were verified attack-by-attack against Mermaid 11.16.1 and must not be weakened.

displayedTextSingleLine.description: Every text that enters the sequence DSL must be single-line: participant.title, message.label, frame.label and branches[].label. Newlines (\n, \r, \r\n) are rejected by the validator and defensively re-asserted by the encoder/generator, because a newline injects a new DSL statement (a new participant, autonumber off, or a parse error — the consequence varies by injection position).
rules: Reject \n, \r and \r\n in participant.title, message.label, frame.label and branches[].label

The encoder must not inject
or any other newline substitute
Regression asserts structure counts (participants, message lines, sequence numbers) unchanged AND original text fully visible

literalTextEncoding.description: Message labels and participant titles (quoted alias context) use Mermaid #code; entity syntax with a 9-character table, implemented as a single-pass character mapping. Chained replace is forbidden: it re-escapes the # and ; its own output introduces. Frame conditions are plain text (no entity encoding) — an entity inside a word wider than a narrow frame gets shredded by wrapLabel and sequence.wrap cannot disable that.
rules: Single-pass character mapping only; chaining .replace calls is forbidden

$ blocks the $$...$$ math-rendering path (would produce foreignObject); : blocks wrap:/nowrap: control prefixes; % blocks %%{...}%% directive deletion, which silently removes text without changing any count
Frame conditions are validated to exclude the same 9 characters and all newlines; the generator re-asserts this defensively (plain-text output, no entity encoding)
Acceptance asserts structure unchanged AND original text fully visible, never merely that the generated string contains an escape sequence
Reject these characters and all newlines in frame.label and branches[].label
Reword the condition or move the fact into a message detail when these characters are needed

messageLabelLength.description: Length is counted in Unicode code points, NOT JavaScript .length (which counts UTF-16 code units).
rules: Above the soft cap the skill prompts to shorten and prefers moving content into detail
Above the hard cap validation rejects the MapSpec
Counting must use code-point iteration (e.g. [...text].length), never .length

messageCount.description: Counted over recursively expanded declared messages (a loop containing two messages counts two, not multiplied by iterations).
rules: Above the soft cap the skill triggers one scope choice (prefer splitting by scenario into multiple maps); 31-60 allowed when the user explicitly needs the full chain
Above the hard cap validation rejects the MapSpec; never silently drop messages

participantIdMapping.description: Participant ids legal per the node-id regex can collide with sequence syntax keywords (end, loop, alt, autonumber, participant) and fail to parse as endpoints. The generator deterministically maps declared order to internal safe ids icm_p1, icm_p2, ... used on the participant line and every endpoint. MapSpec, selection keys, evidence and detail views always use the original id.
rules: No keyword blacklist (unmaintainable)
The generated DSL must not leak an original id as an endpoint
Selection keys are participant:<id> and message:<recursive-path> (e.g. message:2.1), always built from original ids
activatesTo and deactivatesFrom must not both be true on one message
Messages inside frames (loop/opt/alt, any depth) must not carry either activation boolean
An outer activation may wrap whole frames (activate, then any frames without activation, then deactivate) — validated against Mermaid 11.16.1

Pairing is linear over declaration order: each activation must meet a deactivation for the same participant later at the same or an outer level; repeated activation of an already-active participant is rejected; dangling activation or deactivation is rejected
The mapping unit is the message record: the document-order contiguous block (text set, message line, lifeline segment, sequence number) — never a text.messageText count (multi-line texts would split)
Renderer self-check asserts .messageLine0/.messageLine1 count == recursively declared message count and text.sequenceNumber count == the same count
Whole-artifact foreignObject count must be 0 for sequence maps

strictValidationCommand.description: Canonical command to validate a MapSpec against the schema in strict mode. It is pinned through package-lock.json and invoked by tests/mapspec/ajv-strict.mjs.
strictValidationCommand.notes: schema must compile cleanly under ajv strict mode WITH strict-required (no unknown keywords, no required-without-properties). Pinned by package-lock.json: ajv@8.20.0, ajv-cli@5.0.0. build-rules (this file) are enforced by build-html.mjs unit tests, not by ajv.
